message:
Jarvis Lead session handoff (2026-11-05).

Repository: main clean and pushed at 74cc40c. Use canonical Git ledger/repo as authority; refresh when resuming.

Completed/deployed: MCP discovery annotations and descriptions cleanup integrated in 345aea8, production server deployed and SHA256 verified (74d746e279f88f7c4c37f5589e7de8fb8f950cbb75b065eac1e0bf5f87fb34cd). All 99 tools OpenWorld=false and Destructive=false; 19 descriptions simplified.

Integrated, NOT deployed: WriteFile absent-file fix source 45dbc2e, merged in 74cc40c. expectedHash='none' requires nonexistent target; empty means no precondition; SHA256 on missing file gives validation error. Three filesystem tests added. 347 client/90 server Release tests passed. Feedback 3af31ae0f4394bd19db3312082e4bbcf is InProgress pending client/server deployment and live confirmation. Ask operator permission before deploying.

Other open feedback: 2889995a3e19416ab6ea0709d373f699 (OpenAI false positives blocking resume_agent/notify_agent/feedback). No proven Jarvis defect; don't claim solved by metadata.

Next investigation: Can two Jarvis clients run simultaneously on same machine? Verify device ID generation/persistence, server routing and shared workspace/config behavior. Prior read-only rg inspection was blocked by external safety checks, so no conclusion reached. Operator is starting a fresh Lead session; avoid importing extended speculation about safety-check internals.

Workflow: Jarvis tools/worktrees, ordinary team Git workflow, no rebase/cherry-pick, Lead self-reviews Jarvis changes (no separate reviewer), don't launch Codex through Jarvis; seek optimal engineering, no artificial schedule pressure. Always ask before deployment. End turns with actionable 'Next: ...'.

Next: inspect dual-client identity/routing implementation; propose safe configuration and verify.
